intro_html: This Mongolian beef bowl gives you that sweet and savory restaurant flavor without the restaurant bill. Lean ground beef browns fast, then simmers in a honey soy garlic sauce with broccoli and peppers over rice. It runs about $6.48 a serving (at everyday cost) with 43 grams of protein, and it makes 14 bowls.
cost_closing_html: About $6.48 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings delivers 43 grams of protein at 559 calories.
upsell_html: Fifteen minutes of work and you have takeout flavor at a fraction of the cost. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Lean 93/7 ground beef is the priciest part, so shop the sales. Buy ground beef in family packs when it is marked down and freeze in meal-sized portions.
Frozen broccoli is cheaper than fresh and skillet-ready. Keep frozen florets on hand and add them straight to the pan.
Honey and soy sauce season the whole batch for pennies. Buy one bottle of each and they will outlast many meals.
make_it: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks, then drain any grease.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and stir for about a minute.
Pour in the soy sauce and honey and let it bubble into a glaze.
Add the broccoli florets and sliced red pepper and cook until just tender.
Cook the rice while the skillet finishes.
Spoon the saucy beef and vegetables over the rice and serve.
